itemized.page_subtotal_gates: ALL SEVEN page subtotals fired and closed to the cent. Schedule A: p3 rows 25,769.24 = printed 25,769.24; p4 9,625.00 = 9,625.00; p5 3,700.00 = 3,700.00; p6 12,898.93 = 12,898.93; p7 4,960.00 = 4,960.00; the five subtotals sum to the printed grand total 56,953.17. Schedule B: p8 rows 34,837.64 = printed 34,837.64; p9 15,270.14 = 15,270.14; sum = printed grand total 50,107.78.
itemized.escalation_note: none needed - born-digital Excel print, crisp at 200 dpi. Every page was read twice (100 dpi classification pass, then an independent 200 dpi read) with identical results, and all seven page-subtotal gates then closed exactly. No tight cell crop was used, so verified=0 on every row per the brief's strict definition.
itemized.notes: 9-page filing: p1 cover, p2 Summary Page, pp.3-7 'Schedule A - Itemized Contributions Received' (born-digital spreadsheet on the county's own Schedule layout, each page carrying its own 'Subtotal from this page' plus a repeated grand total), pp.8-9 'Schedule B - Itemized Expenditures Made' likewise. This is one of the cleanest filings in the corpus - every subtotal closes. Schedule A has explicit City/State/Zip columns beside a REDACTED Address column, so city/state are real values here (zip discarded per PRIVACY). Schedule A carries its own 'Inkind?' column: 10 rows marked 'in-kind' -> in_kind=true. Those same 10 in-kind items are ALSO listed on Schedule B p9 with '(inkind)' in the Purpose cell and they DO count toward the printed expenditure total (verified: the p9 subtotal only closes with them included) - so the same economic event appears once on each side by the filer's own design, which is a source property, not a double count by us. Note p9's in-kind block is in a smaller font and is date-ordered separately from the block above it. One City cell is clipped by the column width ('Cottonwood H', p7 Rosemary Boyle) and is kept verbatim. GEOMETRY: supplied for the uniform single-line Schedule B rows (pp.8-9); OMITTED on Schedule A because those rows are variable-height (1-3 text lines) and a uniform-grid pointer would be wrong for every row after a tall one.
